releases.title: Main window opens on launch
releases.summary: Fixes "launching the app again shows no window": this is a menu bar resident app, so the process keeps running after the main window is closed, and relaunching previously only activated the instance without showing a window. The main window now always opens on launch; a repeated launch or "Open Wallpaper Library" from the menu bar brings it back to the front.
highlights: The main window always opens at launch (no longer only when the library is empty)
Launching again while the app is running (Spotlight / Finder / open command) reopens the main window automatically
Fixed a matching issue where "Open Wallpaper Library…" in the menu bar could fail to summon the window (SwiftUI windows with hidden title bars are identified by title or scene id)
The app stays resident in the menu bar after the main window is closed — behavior unchanged
notes: The wallpaper engine keeps playing while the window is closed; the menu bar icon can pause, advance to the next wallpaper, or reopen the window at any time

releases.title: UI redesign and video resource management
releases.summary: Rebuilt the overall UI and interactions: sidebar groups with live playback status, library filtering, search and hover actions, new built-in system wallpapers and online video import, plus a new storage page that manages video resource usage and deletion in one place.
highlights: UI redesign: the sidebar is split into "Library / Manage" groups with live playback status at the bottom (playing / auto-pause reason / manually paused)
Library redesign: type filter (all / video / image / dynamic wallpaper), name search, card hover actions (set as wallpaper, add to playlist) and double-click to apply
Dynamic wallpapers are editable: open the editor again from the card's "Edit Schedule" hover action or context menu
Built-in system wallpapers: browse macOS's own dynamic wallpaper videos (e.g. Tahoe Day, Sonoma) in one click; adding by "reference" is recommended so no files are copied and no library space is used
Online video import: paste a direct mp4 / mov link and the downloaded copy joins the library under its original file name
Storage page: media totals, library copy usage and reference counts; per-item source (local import / built-in / online), size, duration and usage context

Delete management: per-item delete with confirmation (copies note reclaimable space, references state the source file is untouched); one-click cleanup of unused video copies; orphan thumbnail cleanup; open resource folder
Fixed leftover thumbnails after deleting media in 0.1.0 — thumbnails are now removed together with the item
New headless maintenance commands: --seed-system-wallpapers and --import-url <url> for scripted batch import
Missing-source detection: items whose source was moved or deleted externally are marked "missing" and playback falls back to the system wallpaper
notes: "Reference" items only record the system file path (e.g. /System/Library/Desktop Pictures); deleting the item never deletes the system file nor frees disk space
"Copy" items live in the library directory (~/Library/Application Support/cduyzhDynamicWallpapaer/Library); deleting them on the storage page permanently frees that space
Online import requires the target site to allow direct downloads; downloaded copies remain subject to the source site's own license (Pexels / Mixkit etc.) — respect their terms

releases.title: First release: video / image / time-based dynamic wallpapers
releases.summary: A native macOS dynamic wallpaper app. Drawing on desktop-level rendering techniques used by open-source dynamic wallpaper apps, it plays looping video, static images, or time-based dynamic wallpapers at the desktop level on every display.
highlights: Desktop-level rendering: a borderless window sits at CGWindowLevelForKey(.desktopWindow), below desktop icons and above the system wallpaper, visible on all Spaces
Video wallpapers: seamless looping via AVQueuePlayer + AVPlayerLooper with 0.5–2× speed, volume and mute controls
Image wallpapers: static images fill each display
Dynamic wallpapers: switch between multiple media by local time of day, wrapping automatically past midnight
Smart pause: pauses when the frontmost app is fullscreen, on battery power, after idle minutes, or when the display sleeps or the screensaver starts
Playlists: sequential or shuffled auto-rotation with optional crossfade
Multi-display: independent enable/disable and wallpaper choice per screen
Hide desktop icons: one-click toggle of Finder's CreateDesktop setting, restorable at any time
Global hotkey: Carbon RegisterEventHotKey toggles play/pause without accessibility permission
Menu bar app: LSUIElement resident status item with the main window opened on demand
Launch at login: registered via SMAppService
notes: First use: open the main window, add a video or image, then click "Set as Wallpaper" on its card
Video wallpapers are muted by default; uncheck mute in settings and adjust the volume to enable sound
Hide desktop icons modifies com.apple.finder's CreateDesktop and restarts Finder; turning the toggle off restores the icons
Fullscreen pause detection reads the frontmost app's window bounds via CGWindowList — no screen-recording permission needed (window content is never read)
